name: Maize Streak Virus
description: A viral disease transmitted by leafhoppers that causes distinctive yellow streaks along leaf veins. It is one of the most damaging viral diseases of maize in Africa.
symptoms: Pale yellow to white streaks along leaf veins
Streaks may coalesce causing chlorosis of entire leaves
Stunted plant growth and reduced vigor
Poor cob development and yield loss
Leaves may appear striped or mottled
causes: Maize streak virus transmitted by Cicadulina leafhoppers
Infection occurring near grassy weeds that harbor the virus
Populations of viruliferous leafhoppers migrating into fields
Late planting coinciding with peak leafhopper activity
treatments: No curative treatment available for viral infection
Control leafhopper vectors with insecticides if caught early
Remove and destroy infected plants to reduce spread
prevention: Plant MSV-resistant maize varieties (e.g., Streak-resistant hybrids)
Control grassy weeds that serve as virus reservoirs
Synchronize planting dates to avoid peak leafhopper populations
Use neem-based botanical sprays as repellent
Intercrop with non-host crops to reduce vector movement
